designGate.prompt: Before writing code, sketch how LRU get/put stay O(1), and what would have to be true later for pin (some keys never evicted) and a swappable eviction policy to plug in without rewriting the value store. Name the eviction seam.

parts.title: LRU cache

hints.text: What bookkeeping answers 'used longest ago' without scanning?
A dict alone has no order. What structure gives lookup and order?
OrderedDict: move_to_end on use, popitem(last=False) to evict.

probes: What happens to eviction order on a put that only updates a key?
Why might production use an explicit DLL + map instead of OrderedDict?

parts.title: Pin / unpin

hints.text: Eviction must skip some keys. Where do pinned keys live relative to your recency structure?
Keep values for everyone; keep the LRU order only for unpinned keys.
pin: remove from order dict. unpin: re-insert as MRU. If order is empty at capacity, all pinned -> ValueError.

probes: Who owns 'cannot be evicted' — the cache or the eviction order?
What should get on a pinned key do to recency?

parts.title: Pluggable policy

hints.text: Cache stores values; policy only ranks evictable keys. Where does pin sit?
set_policy: new_policy.reset(old.ordered_keys()) — pinned keys are not in ordered_keys.
LRUPolicy / LFUPolicy with touch, forget, evict, ordered_keys, reset. LRUCache = Cache(LRUPolicy()).

probes: Why must a swap leave the next eviction unchanged?
How does unpin re-enter the active policy?

criteria: pin blocks eviction; all-pinned put raises
set_policy reseed preserves next victim among evictable keys
Cache vs policy seam; LRUCache reuses Cache
stated why pin is not an eviction policy

provenance.note: Rewritten to match peak_question_bank lrulfucache.py: LRU -> pin -> pluggable policy.
